categories.description: Final exit duration of --nw-tick-out and --nw-tick-out-duration: 100ms times the computed --nw-motion-scale (0, 0.6, 1 or 1.2), still shorter than the enter duration (FR-001, FR-002, T047). They did not exist in v2.1.0. The composite also carries the exit easing cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1). Pinned to :root, to the <missing> old value and to the exact new duration at any of the four scales.

Final exit duration of --nw-sweep-out and --nw-sweep-out-duration: 250ms times the computed --nw-motion-scale (0, 0.6, 1 or 1.2), still shorter than the enter duration (FR-001, FR-002, T047). They did not exist in v2.1.0. The composite also carries the exit easing cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1). Pinned to :root, to the <missing> old value and to the exact new duration at any of the four scales.

Final exit duration of --nw-uplink-out and --nw-uplink-out-duration: 300ms times the computed --nw-motion-scale (0, 0.6, 1 or 1.2), still shorter than the enter duration (FR-001, FR-002, T047). They did not exist in v2.1.0. The composite also carries the exit easing cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1). Pinned to :root, to the <missing> old value and to the exact new duration at any of the four scales.

New motion custom properties on :root: exit composites, duration and easing longhands, stagger and loop cycles, and the --nw-loop-state knob (FR-001, FR-002, FR-006). Existing --nw-tick/--nw-sweep/--nw-uplink are unchanged. The exit composites and durations (--nw-*-out, --nw-*-out-duration) are pinned to their final values by motion-exit-tick, motion-exit-sweep and motion-exit-uplink, which come first. Pinned to :root and to the <missing> old value.

Reduced motion now wins over every intensity level (FR-006, known issue K1): under prefers-reduced-motion, --nw-motion-scale resolves to 0 and --nw-pulse-state and --nw-loop-state to paused, even with data-intensity set. Before, the intensity block won.

Consequence of motion-reduced (FR-006, K1): the existing --nw-tick composite (150ms, cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.7, 1)) multiplies by --nw-motion-scale, so under reduced motion with data-intensity set it computes to calc(150ms * 0) instead of * 0.6 (archive) or * 1.2 (combat). Pinned to :root, to reduced motion on and to the exact old and new composite.

Consequence of motion-reduced (FR-006, K1): the existing --nw-sweep composite (350ms, cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)) multiplies by --nw-motion-scale, so under reduced motion with data-intensity set it computes to calc(350ms * 0) instead of * 0.6 (archive) or * 1.2 (combat). Pinned to :root, to reduced motion on and to the exact old and new composite.

Consequence of motion-reduced (FR-006, K1): the existing --nw-uplink composite (400ms, cubic-bezier(0, 0.6, 0.4, 1)) multiplies by --nw-motion-scale, so under reduced motion with data-intensity set it computes to calc(400ms * 0) instead of * 0.6 (archive) or * 1.2 (combat). Pinned to :root, to reduced motion on and to the exact old and new composite.

Consequence of motion-reduced (FR-006, K1): the universal reduced-motion kill switch in accessibility.css does not reach pseudo-elements, so the switch knob (.switch .track::after) keeps a transition whose duration is --nw-tick. With data-intensity set that was 0.09s (archive) or 0.18s (combat) under reduced motion; it is now 0s.

Closed overlay instances now have a real closed state (FR-004, FR-005, FR-007). Pinned to the parity fixture's closed instances (inside .fixture-closed): drawer, modal and command palette without data-open or with data-open="false", dropdown menu and toast with data-open="false", and a tooltip that is not hovered or focused or is data-open="false". They get pointer-events: none (not the tooltip content, which already had it in v2) and, where the element moves or fades, the closed opacity 0, transform and visibility: hidden. Open, "true" and absent-attribute dropdown and toast instances sit outside the container, so any change to their visibility, opacity, pointer-events or transform is reported as unexpected.

Consequence of motion-overlays (FR-004, FR-005, FR-007): visibility and pointer-events inherit, so everything inside a closed overlay now computes hidden and none instead of visible and auto. This is what takes the contents out of the accessibility tree and out of the tab order. Pinned to the closed instances in .fixture-closed; contents of open overlays must not change.

Closed overlays on the workshop example page get their v3 closed state (FR-004, FR-007): the drawer and its backdrop (data-open="false") and the command palette backdrop (data-open="false"), plus everything inside them, compute pointer-events: none (inherited) and the palette panel sits at translateY(-8px). Pinned to this page and to those three elements by DOM position, since parity paths carry no attributes; the page has no open overlay.

The closed command palette on the synapse-ops example page (no data-open) and everything inside it compute pointer-events: none (FR-004, FR-007). Pinned to this page and to that element by DOM position, since parity paths carry no attributes; the page's own stylesheet hides it with display: none, so nothing else about it changes.

A tooltip with data-open="true" is now open at rest (FR-005, FR-007): in v2 data-open did nothing on a tooltip, so its content stayed at opacity 0 until hover. Pinned to the fixture's open tooltip, which sits directly in a section, outside .fixture-closed, and to the eight base states (four levels, reduced motion off and on); the hover and focus-within cases are their own categories.

A tooltip now opens when focus is inside it (FR-007): v2 only opened on :hover, so with :focus-within forced its content stays at opacity 0 there and is 1 now. Only the forced :focus-within state is matched.

Overlays animate out as well as in (FR-004, FR-007): the overlay transitions now use the exit tokens when closed and the enter tokens when open, with visibility held back by --nw-*-out-duration on the way out. Before, the drawer, modal and command palette shared one --nw-sweep transition for both directions and animated visibility itself, the tooltip used a literal 0.15s, and the dropdown menu and toast had no transition.

The dropdown item hover transition uses --nw-tick instead of a literal 0.15s (FR-003), so it scales with data-intensity and honours reduced motion, and takes the tick easing instead of the default ease.

Component transitions run on --nw-tick instead of literal 0.15s and 0.1s (FR-003, SC-003): buttons (colour, border and the press transform), form inputs, sidebar items, tabs and breadcrumb links. They now scale with data-intensity (0.09s archive, 0.18s combat), take the tick easing instead of the default ease, and the button press transform moves from 0.1s to the tick duration, so press timing joins the motion vocabulary. Property lists and order are unchanged. Under reduced motion nothing differs: the blanket transition: none already won. Pinned to the elements that owned those declarations and to the old and new values.

The button spinner (--nw-loop-spin, 0.8s) is slower at archive (FR-002, Principle V): 0.8s to 1.33333s (0.8s over the 0.6 motion scale), with reduced motion off. Operator is unchanged. Pinned to the workshop page, to the spinner pseudo-element, to archive and to the exact old and new duration; the reduced-motion case is motion-reduced-backstop-workshop.

The button spinner is faster at combat (FR-002, Principle V): 0.8s to 0.666667s (0.8s over the 1.2 motion scale), with reduced motion off. Pinned like motion-loops-spinner-archive, to combat and the exact step.

The skeleton shimmer (--nw-loop-shimmer, 1.2s) is slower at archive (FR-002, Principle V): 1.2s to 2s (over the 0.6 motion scale), with reduced motion off. Operator is unchanged. Pinned to the parity fixture, to the shimmer pseudo-element, to archive and to the exact old and new duration; the reduced-motion case is motion-reduced-backstop.

The skeleton shimmer is faster at combat (FR-002, Principle V): 1.2s to 1s (over the 1.2 motion scale), with reduced motion off. Pinned like motion-loops-shimmer-archive, to combat and the exact step.

The uplink stagger is a multiple of --nw-stagger instead of literal 0.05s steps (FR-003, SC-003), so it scales with data-intensity: 0.03s steps (0.05, 0.1 and 0.15s become 0.03, 0.06 and 0.09s) at archive, 0.05s steps (unchanged) at operator. Only the workshop page uses .uplink, on its first stat strip; parity paths carry no classes beyond the first, so the category is pinned to that page, to the strip's position, to archive and to the three step values.

The uplink stagger is a multiple of --nw-stagger instead of literal 0.05s steps (FR-003, SC-003), so it scales with data-intensity: 0.06s steps (0.05, 0.1 and 0.15s become 0.06, 0.12 and 0.18s) at combat, 0.05s steps (unchanged) at operator. Only the workshop page uses .uplink, on its first stat strip; parity paths carry no classes beyond the first, so the category is pinned to that page, to the strip's position, to combat and to the three step values.

The command palette input had outline: none with no replacement, so keyboard focus was invisible (FR-015, research R12). It now draws a 2px inset --nw-focus-ring outline on :focus-visible (inset because .cmdk clips with overflow: hidden). Only the focused state changes; the unfocused input is untouched.

Checkbox, radio and switch show keyboard focus (FR-015, research R12): their native input is visually hidden, so nothing marked focus. The box or track right after the focused input now draws a 2px --nw-focus-ring outline offset by 2px. The parity tool forces :focus-visible on the input and captures its next siblings, so the box and track are covered. Only the forced :focus-visible state is matched; pinned to the old (no outline) and new values.

A focused segmented-control button draws its focus ring inside the segment (FR-015, research R12): .seg clips with overflow: hidden, so the global outline at offset 2px was cut off. T044 sets the ring in from the segment edge: the outline offset is -4px and a 2px inset band of --nw-text-on-fill (void) sits outside it, so the ring stays distinguishable from the selected segment next to it (its --nw-chrome fill merged with a ring on the edge). The selected segment (aria-pressed) gets a 6px inset band instead, which also keeps the ring off its own fill. Only the forced :focus-visible state is matched; pinned to those values.

Nothing animates under reduced motion (FR-006): the kill switch in accessibility.css now covers ::before and ::after as well as elements, because the universal selector does not reach pseudo-elements. Before, the skeleton shimmer (::after) kept looping under reduced motion. Its animation and transition longhands now take the reset values of animation: none and transition: none. Pinned to the parity fixture, to the skeleton shimmer, to reduced motion on, and to the old and new values.

The same reduced-motion backstop on the workshop example page (FR-006): the button spinner (.btn-loading::before), the checkbox mark, the switch knob, the tab accent and the sidebar accent keep no animation or transition under reduced motion. Pinned to the workshop page, to those pseudo-elements, to reduced motion on, and to the old and new values.

The same reduced-motion backstop on the dashboard example page (FR-006): the legend swatches and the emergency toggle knob declare transition: all on a pseudo-element, which reduced motion now resets to none. Pinned to the dashboard page, to those pseudo-elements, to reduced motion on, and to transition-property all to none.

The same reduced-motion backstop on the neural-ops example page (FR-006): the legend swatches declare transition: all on a pseudo-element, which reduced motion now resets to none. Pinned to the neural-ops page, to those pseudo-elements, to reduced motion on, and to transition-property all to none.

Consequence of motion-reduced-backstop (FR-006): the skeleton shimmer overlay no longer runs, so its transform is none instead of the translateX the animation held it at (the parity harness freezes animations at t=0, which is the -100% start of the sweep). Pinned to the skeleton overlays with reduced motion on.

Uplink content stays visible under reduced motion (FR-006, research R13): .uplink children start at opacity 0 and translateY(4px), and only the animation reveals them. The kill switch removed the animation and left them invisible. Reduced motion now resets them to opacity 1 and no transform. Only the workshop page uses .uplink (its first stat strip); parity paths carry no classes beyond the first, so the category is pinned to that page, to the strip's position and to reduced motion on.

The press shift is now removed under reduced motion (FR-006, fix for a 2.1.0 claim that was false): accessibility.css loads before button.css, so button.css's :active translateY(1px) won at equal specificity and the shift still happened. The reduced-motion rule is now !important. Pinned to buttons, to the forced :active state with reduced motion on, from the translate matrix to none. Parity paths carry no classes beyond the first.
--nw-glow halves at operator (1 → 0.5) and no longer rises at combat (2.2 → 0.5) (FR-013a, FR-013b). Pinned to :root and to the old and new knob values.
--nw-pulse-speed 1.4s → 1.6s, with the combat override (0.7s) removed so combat is faster only through --nw-motion-scale (FR-013a). Pinned to :root and to the old and new speeds.

Consequence of refresh-pulse (FR-013a, T047): the pulsing LEDs of the workshop page read the new --nw-pulse-speed, so with reduced motion off their animation-duration goes from 1.4s to 1.6s at operator and when no level is set. Pinned to the page, to .led, to those two levels and to the exact old and new duration.

Consequence of refresh-pulse (FR-013a, T047) at archive: the pulsing LEDs of the workshop page go from 1.4s to 2.66667s (1.6s over the 0.6 archive motion scale). Pinned to the page, to .led, to archive and to the exact old and new duration.

Consequence of refresh-pulse (FR-013a, T047) at combat: the pulsing LEDs of the workshop page go from 0.7s to 1.33333s (1.6s over the 1.2 combat motion scale), still faster than operator. Pinned to the page, to .led, to combat and to the exact old and new duration.

Consequence of refresh-pulse (FR-013a, T047): the pulsing LEDs of the neural-ops page read the new --nw-pulse-speed, so with reduced motion off their animation-duration goes from 1.4s to 1.6s at operator and when no level is set. Pinned to the page, to .led, to those two levels and to the exact old and new duration.

Consequence of refresh-pulse (FR-013a, T047) at archive: the pulsing LEDs of the neural-ops page go from 1.4s to 2.66667s (1.6s over the 0.6 archive motion scale). Pinned to the page, to .led, to archive and to the exact old and new duration.

Consequence of refresh-pulse (FR-013a, T047) at combat: the pulsing LEDs of the neural-ops page go from 0.7s to 1.33333s (1.6s over the 1.2 combat motion scale), still faster than operator. Pinned to the page, to .led, to combat and to the exact old and new duration.
--nw-text-faint 0.06 → 0.08: quiet dividers and panel edges read a little clearer. Pinned to :root and to the old and new colour.
--nw-text-line and --nw-line 0.12 → 0.14: the general line colour goes one step up. Pinned to :root and to the old and new colour.
--nw-line-strong 0.18 → 0.36: the control-boundary colour reaches 3:1 on --void, --void-warm and --void-panel (FR-014, WCAG 1.4.11). Pinned to :root and to the old and new colour.

New per-surface glow knobs (T033): --nw-led-glow, --nw-control-glow and --nw-progress-glow default to var(--nw-glow) and double at combat, so they resolve to 0 at archive, 0.5 at operator and calc(0.5 * 2) at combat. They did not exist in v2.1.0. Pinned to :root, to <missing> and to those values.
New --nw-hairline knob, 1px: the weight of every structural border. Did not exist in v2.1.0.
New --nw-rule knob, 1.5px: the weight of marks drawn inside controls. Did not exist in v2.1.0.
New --nw-accent-width knob, 2px: one accent weight for tabs, sidebar, diff and toast. Did not exist in v2.1.0.

The toast accent bar goes from 3px to 2px (FR-013, T040): it reads --nw-accent-width, the one accent weight shared with tabs, sidebar and diff. Every other literal border width moved onto --nw-hairline, --nw-rule or --nw-accent-width at the same value, so nothing else changes. Pinned to the left (and inline-start) border width of .toast, 3px to 2px.
New --nw-elevation-overlay token: a neutral, non-coloured shadow for overlays. Did not exist in v2.1.0.

New role tokens --nw-action (the primary action fill), --nw-action-hot (its hover) and --nw-action-text (text on the fill), round 2 of the direction. They did not exist in v2.1.0; their values are the neutral default text colour, the hot chrome blue and void.

State glow moves onto its own knob (FR-013a): .led[data-state] reads --nw-led-glow, which doubles --nw-glow at combat, so a state LED glows 8px at combat (it was 17.6px) while ambient glow no longer rises. At operator the value matches the halved ambient glow and is counted under glow-scale. Pinned to combat, to LEDs, and to the old and new blur.

The command palette and the drawer drop their coloured blur for the neutral --nw-elevation-overlay (FR-013a, research R4, T039). The palette also loses its 1px blue ring layer. At every intensity both now read 0 24px 64px at black 0.7; v2.1.0 scaled a blue blur with the glow knob (0, 1 or 2.2). Pinned to the palette and the drawer and to the exact old and new shadows.

The AI-block heading loses its purple text-shadow (FR-013a, research R4, T039). The shadow inherits, so the heading's own spans (dot, LED, label) lose it too. Pinned to the heading and its child spans and to the exact old shadows (blur 0, 6 or 13.2px: the glow knob at archive, operator and combat) and the new none.

Every glow that reads --nw-glow halves at operator and when no level is set (FR-013b): the knob went 1 → 0.5, so the blur scales by half. Archive is unchanged (0 → 0). Box shadows. Pinned to the component elements that still read --nw-glow (steps, progress fill, LEDs, checkbox, radio and switch marks, segmented text), to the state, and to shadow-shaped old and new values.

Every glow that reads --nw-glow halves at operator and when no level is set (FR-013b): the knob went 1 → 0.5, so the blur scales by half. Archive is unchanged (0 → 0). Text shadows. Pinned to the component elements that read --nw-glow (the pressed segment text), to the state, and to shadow-shaped old and new values.

State glow moves onto the per-component knobs (FR-013, research R4, T038): the current and done step, the checked check, radio and switch marks and the pressed segment read --nw-control-glow, the progress fill reads --nw-progress-glow. Both double --nw-glow at combat, so at combat they glow 6px (4px for the progress fill) where v2.1.0 had 13.2px (8.8px): weaker than v2.1.0, and twice the operator value, because only state signals may rise at combat (FR-013a). Operator and archive are unchanged by the knob, so they stay under glow-scale-operator. Pinned to combat, to those six elements and to the exact old and new blur.

Page-local status glow follows --nw-glow instead of a literal blur (FR-013b, T047): the synapse-ops status dots (.dot), event dots (.ev-dot) and hot risk bar (.rbar-fill) and the neural-ops layer bars (.layer-fill) had a fixed 4px glow at every intensity. They now read calc(4px * var(--nw-glow)), so with --nw-glow at 0.5 they glow 2px at operator and when no level is set, and nothing at archive (unchanged there). Pinned to those two pages (the -ops example pages), to those elements, to box-shadow, to none and operator, and to the exact 4px to 2px step. The purple dot (6px) is examples-glow-scale-operator-purple.

The purple status dot of synapse-ops (.dot.p) had a fixed 6px glow and now reads calc(6px * var(--nw-glow)): 6px to 3px at operator and when no level is set (FR-013b, T047). Pinned like examples-glow-scale-operator, to the purple colour and the exact step.

Same change as examples-glow-scale-operator at combat (FR-013a, FR-013b, T047): --nw-glow is 2.2 in v2.1.0 and 0.5 now, so the 4px page-local glow was 8.8px at combat and is 2px, equal to its operator value. Nothing that is not a state signal glows more at combat than at operator. Pinned to the same pages and elements, to combat and to the exact 8.8px to 2px step.
The purple dot at combat (FR-013a, T047): 6px read 13.2px under the 2.2 knob and is 3px now, equal to operator. Pinned to the purple colour and the exact step.

The workshop page modal box takes the neutral --nw-elevation-overlay in place of a blue glow (FR-013a, T047), like the library .modal. The page rule is now var(--nw-elevation-overlay); v2.1.0 does not define that token, so on that side the declaration is invalid and the shadow computes to none. Pinned to the workshop page, to box-shadow on the modal box, from none to the token value.
Quiet dividers and panel edges read a little clearer (FR-014 direction): --nw-text-faint 0.06 → 0.08. Every colour property that resolves to the token changes; pinned to the old and new colour.
One step up for the general line colour: --nw-text-line and --nw-line 0.12 → 0.14. Every colour property that resolves to the token changes; pinned to the old and new colour.
Control boundaries reach 3:1 on the black surfaces (FR-014, WCAG 1.4.11): --nw-line-strong 0.18 → 0.36. Every colour property that resolves to the token changes; pinned to the old and new colour.

The workshop page prints --nw-glow in its HUD, so the readout text, and with it the HUD box and its fixed-position origin, change width when the knob goes 1 → 0.5. Pinned to that page and to the HUD and its second item.

Decorative glow is removed from the board set at every intensity (FR-013a, research R4): the resting box-shadow of .btn-success and .btn-ai, the .stat-value text-shadow and the .m-value text-shadow of .metric-cell and its highlight. Pinned to the property, to each old coloured shadow (any blur, because the blur scaled with the glow knob) and to the new value none.

Consequence of glow-decor (FR-013a), settled by T039: on the synapse-ops example page a metric value also carries the .glow-green utility, which the hardcoded .m-value text-shadow used to override. With that shadow gone the utility shows, and since T039 it scales with --nw-glow and is weaker: 0.33 and 0.13 alpha at 4px and 8px at operator and combat (the v2.1.0 text-shadow was 0.4 and 0.15 at a fixed 6px and 12px), none at archive. Pinned to the page, to the .m-value in a .metric-cell, and to the exact old and new shadows.

The .glow-* utilities stay opt-in but become restrained and scaled by --nw-glow (FR-013b, research R4, T039): the blurs are calc(8px * glow) and calc(16px * glow), and the alphas drop by about a third (0.5 to 0.33, 0.2 to 0.13, red 0.3 to 0.2). At operator and combat that is 4px and 8px, clearly weaker than v2.1.0's fixed 8px and 16px; at archive the blur is 0. Pinned to the coverage page spans that carry a .glow-* class, and to the exact old and new shadows.

The panel header background-image (a blue gradient, plus scanlines at combat) is removed (FR-013a). Every background longhand of the header resolves to its initial layer list: none for the image and, since the two-layer list collapses to one, one value instead of two for the other longhands. Pinned to .panel-header.

match.old: ^(none, none|none, linear-gradient\(rgba\(102, 153, 255, 0\.06\), rgba\(0, 0, 0, 0\) 80%\)|repeating-linear-gradient\(0deg, rgba\(102, 153, 255, 0\.05\) 0px, rgba\(102, 153, 255, 0\.05\) 1px, rgba\(0, 0, 0, 0\) 1px, rgba\(0, 0, 0, 0\) 3px\), linear-gradient\(rgba\(102, 153, 255, 0\.18\), rgba\(0, 0, 0, 0\) 70%\)|scroll, scroll|normal, normal|border-box, border-box|padding-box, padding-box|0% 0%, 0% 0%|repeat, repeat|auto, auto)$

categories.description: The two header decoration knobs are deleted (FR-013a, T037): --nw-header-gradient and --nw-header-pattern leave :root and every intensity block, so each resolves to <missing>. Nothing reads them since the panel header background-image went (decor-removal). Pinned to :root, the two names and their exact v2.1.0 values. The migration guide entry comes with T055.

Header rules go neutral (direction round 2): the bottom border of .panel-header, .modal-header and .nw-table th goes from the solid --nw-primary-dim to --nw-line (white at 0.14). Round 1 had --nw-line-chrome; the maintainer rejected it as too close to v2.1.0. The chrome colour is gone from the rule and the label text is neutral too. Pinned to the bottom border colour of those elements and to the old and new colour.

Form controls get a 3:1 boundary (FR-014, WCAG 1.4.11): the border of input, select and textarea goes from --nw-text-line (0.12) to --nw-line-strong (0.36). Pinned to those elements and to the old and new colour; the fixture carries one of each.
Placeholder text reaches AA (FR-014): opacity 0.6 → 0.75 on the --nw-text-dim colour, 3.64:1 → 5.03:1 on --void-panel. Pinned to the ::placeholder pseudo-element and to the old and new opacity.
.modal takes the neutral --nw-elevation-overlay shadow (it had none). Pinned to .modal, to the old none and to the new shadow.

An open modal computes transform none instead of scale(1), like .cmdk (no residual transform, crisp text). Pinned to .modal, to the old identity matrix and to none; the closed modal keeps scale(0.96).

Labels go neutral (direction round 2, FR-013a): .panel-header, .modal-header, .modal-title, .nw-table th, .stat .stat-label, .metric-cell .m-label and .field-label change from the blue chrome colour to --nw-text-mute (#aaaaaa), and so does everything that follows the label colour (inherited text, currentColor borders, outlines and carets on the label and its descendants). Pinned to those elements and to blue to #aaaaaa; the kanji inside a header has its own category.

A .kanji inside .panel-header or .modal-header with no colour of its own takes --nw-text-default (#e6e6e6), the one bright mark in a quiet header. The default is set inside :where(), so a colour utility on the kanji itself and inline styles still win; only a colour inherited from an ancestor loses to it. The one case in the parity pages is the workshop Fleet Pulse header, where the kanji inherited #aaaaaa from an inline-styled wrapper span. Pinned to the exact chain panel-header, wrapper span, .kanji, to that page, from #aaaaaa to #e6e6e6.
The .panel border goes from --nw-text-faint (0.06 in v2.1.0) to --nw-line (0.14), a neutral hairline that reads against the page. Pinned to .panel and the four sides, old and new colour.
The .modal border goes from the solid --nw-primary-dim to --nw-line-strong (white at 0.36, the 3:1 control boundary). Pinned to .modal, to the old and new colour.
The .modal-footer top rule goes from --nw-text-faint (0.06) to --nw-line (0.14), matching the header rule. Pinned to .modal-footer, its top border, old and new colour.

Table cell text is content, not a data readout: .nw-table td goes from --nw-green to --nw-text-default (#e6e6e6), including the colours that follow currentColor. The data colour stays on stat and metric values. Pinned to td (with any utility class), old green to #e6e6e6.

Consequence of round2-table-text on the data-table example (T045): the progress bar, its fill and the LED sit inside a td and take no colour of their own, so everything that follows currentColor on them (borders, outlines, carets, text decoration) moves with the cell text from --nw-green to --nw-text-default (#e6e6e6). Their own colours (fill background, LED state) are unchanged. Pinned to the data-table page, to .nw-progress, its .nw-progress-fill and .led directly inside a td, old green to #e6e6e6.

Consequence of round2-table-text on the dashboard example (T045): the strategy progress bars, their fill and the LEDs sit inside a td and take no colour of their own, so everything that follows currentColor on them (borders, outlines, carets, text decoration) moves with the cell text from --nw-green to --nw-text-default (#e6e6e6). Their own colours (fill background, LED state) are unchanged. Pinned to the dashboard page, to .nw-progress, its .nw-progress-fill and .led directly inside a td, old green to #e6e6e6.
